title: "Composition: SAE's rollout and who enters the over-demanded schools"
output: html_document
params:
  data_dir: !r file.path(ifelse(Sys.getenv("USERPROFILE") != "", Sys.getenv("USERPROFILE"), path.expand("~")), "Dropbox", "Effect SAE on SUA", "data", "finalized_design_v1", "composition")
  out_dir: "output"
  cores: 0
---

This notebook produces the composition part of *Effect of Centralized School Choice on College
Admissions Outcomes* (Rios, Larroucau and Marar): the paper's access section ("Centralized
Assignment and Access to Over-Demanded Schools"), on who enters the over-demanded schools before
and after SAE's staggered rollout, and that section's appendix. It writes the tables and figures of
the access section and its appendix, Appendix Table B.8 included, and three macro files (two of the
numbers quoted in their text, one of Appendix Table B.7's estimates, which the paper inputs without
printing), under the names and relative paths the paper uses:

| File | Exhibit |
|---|---|
| `tables/lottery_od_historical_records.tex` | Table I: the over-demanded schools' graduates before SAE against the other SAE schools' |
| `tables/alloc_headline.tex` | Table II: SAE's effect on the entering classes' prior-year GPA and low-income share |
| `figures/alloc_event_study.pdf`, `figures/alloc_event_study_prio.pdf` | Figure 2's two panels: the event studies of the two outcomes |
| `tables/lottery_od_historical_macros.tex` | the macros the section's text and Appendix Table B.1 print (Table I's measures, the schools' counts, the value-added sample) |
| `tables/entrant_count_macros.tex` | macros of Appendix Table B.7's estimates (the paper inputs the file; its text prints none of them) |
| `tables/composition_text_macros.tex` | the rows of `numbers/composition_text_numbers.csv` as macros (the Introduction prints two of them) |
| `tables/lottery_od_historical_va_coverage.tex` | Appendix Table B.1: the coverage of the historical value-added estimates |
| `tables/lottery_od_historical_va_checks.tex` | Appendix Table B.2: school value added under alternative specifications |
| `tables/appendix14_a1_allocation.tex` | Appendix Table B.3: checks on the change in entrant composition |
| `tables/appendix14_a2_intake.tex` | Appendix Table B.4: the number of entrants and the share with prior-year grades |
| `tables/appendix_ninth_grade_composition.tex` | Appendix Table B.5: entering-class composition at ninth-grade entry |
| `tables/appendix_ninth_grade_profiles.tex` | Appendix Table B.6: entrants and lottery compliers in the supported ninth-grade cohorts |
| `tables/appendix_entrant_counts.tex` | Appendix Table B.7: entrant counts by low-income status |
| `tables/appendix_alloc_event_study.tex` | Appendix Table B.8: entering-class composition in the first two years of SAE (the first two SAE-assigned classes) |

Each table and macro file starts with the line `% Generated by composition.Rmd`. The folder
`numbers/` holds the notebook's csvs: every estimate above at full precision, the numbers the text
quotes (`composition_text_numbers.csv`, one row per number, named as the text's macros) and each
statement the current text makes about these results, checked (`text_claims.csv`).

**The design.** A school-grade (a grade within a school) is over-demanded when it offered seats in
at least one SAE process of 2016-2021 and, in each such process, its effective demand exceeded its
seats in every one of 2,000 recorded reruns of SAE's main stage with new lottery numbers. The
project's pipeline then applies the school and entrant rules listed below. The panel holds 10,027
such school-grades; their ninth grades are the 1,020 over-demanded schools of the lottery analysis. Each estimate is did's group-time average effect
(Callaway and Sant'Anna 2021) with not-yet-treated comparison cells, a universal base period ($g-1$)
and no anticipation; standard errors come from did's multiplier bootstrap clustered by region, and
the significance stars from the studentized randomization test over the saved reassignments of SAE's
rollout across the 16 regions.

**Inputs.** The data folder (`params$data_dir`) holds five items, each listed with its bytes and MD5
in `data_manifest.csv` beside this notebook; the notebook checks that the data folder's own
`data_manifest.csv` is the same and every file against the manifest before it reads any, and stops
when a manifest or a file is missing or differs:

- `composition_panel.rds`: one row per entrant child-year in an over-demanded school-grade,
  academic years 2012-2023; 1,707,775 rows, 10,027 school-grades. Its columns are listed in the data
  dictionary below.
- `composition_schools.rds`: one row per school of the historical comparison, 2,533 schools, 1,020
  of them over-demanded (Table I and Appendix Tables B.1 and B.2).
- `composition_applicants.rds`: one row per child of the lottery analysis, 316,538 children
  (Appendix Table B.6).
- `draws/did/regional/`: 16 files of saved reassignments of SAE's rollout across the 16 regions,
  9,999 or 2,999 each, that the randomization tests score.
- `data_manifest.csv`: the manifest, the same as the one beside this notebook.

did draws the bootstrap multipliers anew from the seeds below; the notebook keeps each draw in a
folder of the R session's temporary directory while it runs.

**Command.** From the folder that holds this notebook, with the data folder at its default place
(the coauthors' shared Dropbox folder, `<home>/Dropbox/Effect SAE on SUA/data/finalized_design_v1/
composition/`, `<home>` being `USERPROFILE` on Windows and the home folder elsewhere):

    Rscript -e "knitr::knit('composition.Rmd')"

or, with another data folder or output folder,

    Rscript -e "params <- list(data_dir = '<data folder>', out_dir = '<output folder>'); knitr::knit('composition.Rmd')"

(`rmarkdown::render('composition.Rmd', params = list(...))` reads the same parameters; pandoc is
needed only for its html page). Inside an `Rscript -e` string, write a Windows path with forward
slashes (`C:/Users/...`): R reads a backslash in a string as the start of an escape. A relative
`data_dir` or `out_dir` is read from this notebook's folder, whatever folder the chunks run in
(RStudio's Knit Directory setting, `rmarkdown::render`'s `knit_root_dir`). The knit writes
`composition.md` (code, printed results, warnings and messages) and the output folder
(`params$out_dir`, default `output/` beside this notebook): `tables/`, `figures/` and `numbers/`.
`params$cores` sets the number of processes (0: every core). The notebook writes nothing outside the
output folder and the R session's temporary directory.

**Versions.** The notebook stops unless R is 4.5.1 and did is 2.1.2, and stops when fixest is older
than 0.14.2 (it prints a message when fixest is newer). It also checks did's bootstrap multipliers:
in each draw of its multiplier bootstrap, did gives each of the 16 regions a multiplier of +1 or -1,
drawn by BMisc, and multiplies the regions' influence functions by them. From the main seed
(`SEED_MAIN`), the setup draws the multipliers of one full call, 10,000 draws for the 16 regions
(the call did makes first in Table II's prior-year GPA fit), and stops unless the MD5 of their
160,000 signs is that of these results' multipliers. The check covers the multipliers of that call;
the influence functions come from did, which must be 2.1.2. The versions these results were run
under are in `README.md`; the notebook prints the versions it runs with. On a processor with
performance and efficiency cores (these results: an Intel Core Ultra 7 265), the standard errors,
interval bounds and group-time estimates in the full-precision csvs of `numbers/` can differ from one
knit to the next by relative amounts below 1e-12; every table and macro file is the same. The cell IDs follow the R session's collation order of the labels
`rbd|cod_nivel` (`English_United States.utf8` on Windows when these results were built); another
collation orders the cells differently, which can move the last digits of the estimates and
standard errors. `README.md` records the run time and memory.

**The rules the panel embodies.** The project's pipeline built the panel from the administrative
records under these rules:

- *Over-demanded school-grades.* The rule above: seats in at least one SAE process of 2016-2021,
  and in each such process effective demand above the seats in every one of the 2,000 recorded
  reruns of the main stage.
- *Schools left out.* A school that moves between publicly funded and fee-paying status at any
  point in 2012-2025, read from the dependency code on its students' year-end records, is left out
  whole.
- *Grades.* Every youth secondary program's census rows carry their grade, including the program
  codes SAE's applicant file does not list.
- *Entrants.* An entrant is a child in the school's census in year $t$ who is absent from that
  school's census in year $t-1$, in any of its programs.
- *Prior-year GPA.* Each entrant's GPA of year $t-1$ is the mean of her graded year-end records that
  year (GPA from 1 to 7), standardized over every graded student in Chile that year, one value per
  student; a record without a student ID counts as its own value.

The notebook's own code applies four more: the GPA outcome covers entrants to grades 2-12 (the
PreKinder, Kinder and 1st-grade cell-years are left blank), the Observations rows count the
cell-years of 2012-2020 (the years the estimates use), Appendix Table B.3 has seven rows (the main
estimate, five robustness specifications and the restricted sample), and the largest GPA lead is
recorded against 0.03 SD. The fifth robustness specification, "Reference period $g-2$" (Appendix
Table B.3's sixth row), compares each SAE-assigned class with the class of $g-2$ and covers the
entering classes of 2017-2019; every other estimate compares with the class of $g-1$.

**Data dictionary.** The composition panel (one row per entrant child-year):

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `MRUN` | the child's student ID (the census's own name) |
| `AGNO` | the academic year $t$ of the census in which she enters |
| `RBD` | the school's ID (the census's own name) |
| `COD_NIVEL` | the grade she enters: -1 PreKinder, 0 Kinder, 1-8 grades 1-8, 9-12 secondary grades 1-4 |
| `REGION` | the school's region, 1-16 (13 is the Metropolitan Region) |
| `IS_ENTRY` | 1 for the grades a child usually enters a school at (PreKinder, Kinder, 1, 7 and 9) |
| `DOOR` | the year of the first SAE admission process with offers in the cell's region and grade; that process assigns the class entering in `DOOR + 1` |
| `SLACK_FAIL` | TRUE when the pre-adoption enrollment check flags the cell: the grade's mean enrollment in the four years up to `DOOR` is below 90% of its mean in the three years after, while the school's enrollment shows no such rise (Appendix Table B.3's row "Pre-SAE demand restriction") |
| `DOOR_YEAR_TAG` | TRUE when the cell turned applicants away in its first SAE process (carried for reference; no exhibit here uses it) |
| `PRIO` | 1 when the child is on the low-income (prioritario) roster of year $t$ |
| `PRIOR_GPA_Z` | her prior-year GPA, as defined above; NA when she has no graded record in $t-1$ |
| `N_PRIOR_RECORDS` | the number of her graded records in $t-1$ (NA when none) |
| `UNKNOWN_SCHOOL`, `UNKNOWN_REGION`, `UNKNOWN_GRADE`, `UNKNOWN_CALENDAR` | TRUE when one of her records of $t-1$ lacks a school, the school's region, a grade, or the first SAE process of that region and grade |
| `EXPOSURE_KNOWN` | TRUE when none of the four is missing for any of her records of $t-1$ |
| `EXPOSED` | TRUE when one of her records of $t-1$ was earned in a region and grade SAE already covered |
| `SIGNATURE` | the regions and entry-grade status of her records of $t-1$ (used to recompute `EXPOSED` under each reassigned rollout) |
| `ELIGIBLE_HISTORY` | `EXPOSURE_KNOWN` and not `EXPOSED`: her prior-year grades were earned before SAE reached the region and grade of her prior-year records (the sample of Appendix Table B.3's last row) |

The school file (one row per school; the columns Table I and Appendix Tables B.1 and B.2 read):

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `RBD` | the school's ID |
| `IN_CATALOGUE` | TRUE for a school of the historical comparison: 9th-grade seats in an SAE process of 2016-2021, under the rules the composition appendix states |
| `IS_OD` | TRUE for the 1,020 over-demanded schools |
| `GROUP` | `od` or `other_sae` for a school of the comparison; missing outside it |
| `IS_HISTORICAL`, `IS_COMMON` | TRUE when the school has graduates in the classes of 2012-2015; TRUE when it has every measure of Table I and a value added |
| `NEM_PERCENTILE_MEAN`, `LM_PERCENTILE_MEAN` | its 2012-2015 graduates' mean NEM and reading--mathematics percentiles |
| `ASSIGNED_ANY_MEAN`, `ASSIGNED_TOP10_MEAN`, `ASSIGNED_TOP25_MEAN`, `ASSIGNED_TOP50_MEAN` | the share of those graduates assigned a seat in the centralized college admission system, and a seat in the most selective 10%, 25% and 50% of programs (%) |
| `VA_<FIT>`, `VA_N_<FIT>`, `SIGMA_E_M_<FIT>` | the school's value added and its students in each value-added fit of Appendix Table B.2 (`HEAD` the main one), and the fit's residual SD |
| `COMPLETIONS_2013`, `COMPLETIONS_2015`, `TAKERS_2013`, `TAKERS_2015`, `LINKED_2013`, `LINKED_2015`, `STAYERS` | the class's graduates, those who took the PSU, those in the value-added sample (linked to their 8th-grade SIMCE), and the sample students tested in 8th grade at the same school |

The lottery applicants (one row per child of the lottery analysis; the columns Appendix Table B.6
reads):

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `YEAR`, `MRUN` | the SAE process she applied in (she enters 9th grade in `YEAR + 1`) and her student ID |
| `LOTTERY_SAMPLE` | TRUE when her chance of an offer at an over-demanded school is strictly between 0 and 1 |
| `OFFER`, `D_OD` | 1 when SAE's main stage offered her a seat at one of the 1,020 over-demanded schools; 1 when she attends one of them |
| `CHANCE_GROUP` | her chance of an offer, in hundredths |
| `GPA8_Z`, `PRIORITARIO` | her 8th-grade average (SD) and her low-income status in the application year |
| `ENTRY_RBD` | the school she attends in the entry year (missing without a record) |
| `OD_CHOICES` | the over-demanded schools she ranked in the main stage, continuity options SAE added included, each once |

Names the notebook builds: a *cell* is a school-grade (`rbd|cod_nivel`), with an integer `cell_id`;
the cell-year panel holds `n_ent` (entrants), `n_gpa` (entrants with a prior-year GPA), `gpa_z`
(their mean prior-year GPA), `sh_prio` (the low-income share) and `w_ent` (the cell's mean `n_ent`,
the weight of the entrant-weighted row); `G = DOOR + 1` is the cell's adoption year $g$, the
academic year of the first class SAE assigns; a region's *wave* is the `DOOR` of its entry grades
(SAE reached a region's other grades a year later), and the rollout's four waves hold 1, 4, 10 and
1 regions.

## Setup

Loads the packages, checks the R, did and fixest versions, reads the parameters, sets the seeds and
the draw counts, checks the bootstrap multipliers of a full call from the main seed against these
results', and sets the folders. The random-number state is set from these seeds before each
estimate. A failed check stops the knit, in this chunk (its header sets `error = FALSE`) and in
every later one.

```{r setup, error = FALSE}
library(data.table)
library(did)
library(fixest)
library(parallel)
library(tools)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = TRUE, message = TRUE, error = FALSE)   # every later chunk stops the knit on an error
options(warn = 1)
say <- function(...) { message(sprintf(...)); invisible(NULL) }
KNIT_START <- Sys.time() - 2   # the chunk outputs checks that this knit wrote every output (two seconds for a file system's coarse clock)

# R 4.5.1 and did 2.1.2 are required: did's bootstrap standard errors differ across did versions. fixest 0.14.2 or later is required
# (the version these results were checked with; fixest runs the 2SLS check of Appendix Table B.6's complier means); a newer fixest is
# named in a message
REQUIRED_R <- "4.5.1"
REQUIRED_DID <- "2.1.2"
local({
  r_now <- paste(R.version$major, R.version$minor, sep = ".")
  bad <- c(if (r_now != REQUIRED_R) sprintf("R %s (required: %s)", r_now, REQUIRED_R),
           if (as.character(packageVersion("did")) != REQUIRED_DID)
             sprintf("did %s (required: %s)", packageVersion("did"), REQUIRED_DID))
  if (length(bad)) stop(sprintf("this notebook needs R %s and did %s: ", REQUIRED_R, REQUIRED_DID), paste(bad, collapse = "; "),
                        call. = FALSE)
})
if (packageVersion("fixest") < "0.14.2")
  stop("fixest 0.14.2 or later is required (this is ", packageVersion("fixest"), "): the version these results were checked with",
       call. = FALSE)
if (packageVersion("fixest") > "0.14.2")
  message("fixest ", packageVersion("fixest"), " is newer than 0.14.2, the version these results were checked with")
say("R %s.%s; did %s; BMisc %s; RcppArmadillo %s; data.table %s; fixest %s; knitr %s", R.version$major, R.version$minor,
    packageVersion("did"), packageVersion("BMisc"), packageVersion("RcppArmadillo"), packageVersion("data.table"),
    packageVersion("fixest"), packageVersion("knitr"))
say("collation: %s (the cell IDs follow it)", Sys.getlocale("LC_COLLATE"))

# the parameters: data_dir (the data folder), out_dir (the output folder) and cores (the processes; 0: every core). Knitted
# without them (knitr::knit), each takes its default: the data folder in the coauthors' shared Dropbox folder (under USERPROFILE
# on Windows, the home folder elsewhere), output/ beside this notebook, every core
home <- ifelse(Sys.getenv("USERPROFILE") != "", Sys.getenv("USERPROFILE"), path.expand("~"))
PARAM_DEFAULTS <- list(data_dir = file.path(home, "Dropbox", "Effect SAE on SUA", "data", "finalized_design_v1", "composition"),
                       out_dir = "output", cores = 0L)
if (exists("params"))
  stopifnot("the parameters are data_dir, out_dir and cores" = all(names(params) %in% names(PARAM_DEFAULTS)))
param <- function(name) {
  value <- if (exists("params") && !is.null(params[[name]])) params[[name]] else PARAM_DEFAULTS[[name]]
  stopifnot("one value per parameter" = length(value) == 1L && !is.na(value))
  value
}

# A statement the current text makes about a result, each named by the part of the paper that makes it: each is evaluated (an
# error counts as not holding) and recorded with whether it holds in TEXT_CLAIMS (the chunk text-numbers writes them to
# numbers/text_claims.csv); each that does not hold is printed (a sentence of the text that moves with these results), and once
# all are written the chunk text-numbers stops the knit if any does not hold
new_claims_store <- function() { s <- new.env(parent = emptyenv()); s$rows <- vector("list", 64L); s$n <- 0L; s }
TEXT_CLAIMS <- new_claims_store()
text_claims <- function(..., .store = TEXT_CLAIMS) {
  labels <- ...names()
  stopifnot("every statement carries its label" = ...length() > 0L && !is.null(labels) && all(nzchar(labels)))
  for (i in seq_len(...length())) {
    holds <- isTRUE(tryCatch(...elt(i), error = function(e) NA))
    stopifnot("the statements' record has room" = .store$n < length(.store$rows))
    .store$n <- .store$n + 1L
    .store$rows[[.store$n]] <- data.table(statement = labels[i], holds = holds)
    if (!holds) say("a statement of the current text does not hold with these results: %s", labels[i])
  }
  invisible(NULL)
}
local({   # self-test, on a store of its own: a true, a false and an erroring statement are recorded as TRUE, FALSE, FALSE and the
          # knit goes on; an unlabelled statement stops
  stops <- function(expr) inherits(tryCatch(expr, error = function(e) e), "error")
  s <- new_claims_store()
  suppressMessages(text_claims("t1" = TRUE, "t2" = FALSE, "t3" = stop("an error"), .store = s))   # its two notes not printed
  ok <- s$n == 3L && identical(rbindlist(s$rows[1:3])$holds, c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE)) &&
    identical(rbindlist(s$rows[1:3])$statement, c("t1", "t2", "t3")) && stops(text_claims(TRUE, .store = s))
  stopifnot("text_claims self-test: true, false and an error recorded; an unlabelled statement stops" = ok && TEXT_CLAIMS$n == 0L)
})

# seeds and draw counts (RI, in names such as B_RI and ri_p, stands for randomization inference: the
# tests over the saved reassignments of the rollout)
SEED_MAIN <- 20260815       # Table II, Appendix Table B.4 and Figure 2's GPA panel
SEED_ROBUST <- 20260806     # Appendix Table B.3, rows 2-6 (row 6 the reference-period specification; both columns restart it)
SEED_PRIO_ES <- 20260830    # Figure 2's low-income panel
SEED_PRIOR <- 20260915L     # Appendix Table B.3, last row
SEED_NINTH <- 20261018L     # Appendix Table B.5: its four fits use SEED_NINTH + 1 to + 4, in the table's order
SEED_COUNTS <- 20261018L    # Appendix Table B.7, Panel A: each of the four fits restarts it
B_BOOT <- 10000             # bootstrap draws: Table II, Figure 2, Appendix Table B.4, Appendix Table B.3's last row
B_BOOT_ROBUST <- 999        # bootstrap draws: Appendix Table B.3, rows 2-6
B_RI <- 9999L               # saved rollout reassignments: Table II and Appendix Table B.3's last row
B_RI_ROBUST <- 2999L        # saved reassignments: Appendix Table B.3 rows 2-6, Appendix Table B.4, the joint lead tests
# the paired estimate the randomization test studentizes uses the cells observed in both years of
# each comparison; did also uses cells observed in one year. Each paired estimate must stay this
# close to did's (prior-year GPA in SD; low-income share as a proportion)
TRACK_TOL <- c(gpa_z = 0.02, sh_prio = 0.005)
# the paired leads g-6 .. g-2 (the joint lead test's statistic) must stay this close to did's dynamic leads
LEADS_TRACK_TOL <- 0.02
LEAD_LIMIT_SD <- 0.03       # the largest GPA lead is recorded against this size (gpa_leads_check.csv)

# did's bootstrap multipliers: in each draw of its multiplier bootstrap, did gives each region a multiplier of +1 or -1, drawn with
# BMisc::multiplier_bootstrap from R's random-number stream, and multiplies the regions' influence functions by them (the influence
# functions are did's own; did 2.1.2 is required above). The check draws the multipliers of one full call from the seed SEED_MAIN: B_BOOT
# (10,000) draws for the 16 regions, the call did makes first in Table II's prior-year GPA fit. Each draw is written as a string of 16
# signs (+ for +1, - for -1); the first three strings must be MULTIPLIER_SIGNS, and the MD5 of the 10,000 strings joined in draw order
# with no separator (160,000 characters) must be MULTIPLIER_DIGEST, the digest of these results' multipliers. A BMisc, RcppArmadillo or
# random-number generator that draws other multipliers would change every bootstrap SE, and stops the knit. The session's
# random-number state is left as it was
MULTIPLIER_SIGNS <- c("+++-+--+-++---+-", "+----+++---+-+--", "--++-----++-+---")
MULTIPLIER_DIGEST <- "deed5b8dc6b670f64f561aa319c06d6f"
local({
  saved <- if (exists(".Random.seed", envir = .GlobalEnv, inherits = FALSE)) get(".Random.seed", envir = .GlobalEnv) else NULL
  on.exit(if (is.null(saved)) rm(".Random.seed", envir = .GlobalEnv) else assign(".Random.seed", saved, envir = .GlobalEnv))
  set.seed(SEED_MAIN)
  weights <- BMisc::multiplier_bootstrap(diag(16L), B_BOOT) * 16
  signs <- apply(weights, 1L, function(w) paste(ifelse(w > 0, "+", "-"), collapse = ""))
  digest <- unname(tools::md5sum(bytes = charToRaw(paste(signs, collapse = ""))))
  if (!(identical(dim(weights), c(as.integer(B_BOOT), 16L)) && all(abs(abs(weights) - 1) < 1e-12) &&
        identical(signs[1:3], MULTIPLIER_SIGNS) && identical(digest, MULTIPLIER_DIGEST)))
    stop(sprintf(paste("did's bootstrap multipliers drawn from the seed differ from those of these results (the MD5 of their signs: %s;",
                       "these results': %s; BMisc %s, RcppArmadillo %s, random-number generator %s): every bootstrap SE would differ"),
                 digest, MULTIPLIER_DIGEST, packageVersion("BMisc"), packageVersion("RcppArmadillo"), paste(RNGkind(), collapse = ", ")),
         call. = FALSE)
})
say("did's bootstrap multipliers: the %s draws of the 16 regions from the seed %d are these results' (the MD5 of their signs: %s)",
    format(B_BOOT, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE), SEED_MAIN, MULTIPLIER_DIGEST)

# folders: the data folder; the output folder with tables/ and figures/ (the paper's files) and numbers/ (this notebook's csvs). A
# relative path is read from this notebook's own folder, whatever folder the chunks run in (RStudio's Knit Directory setting,
# rmarkdown::render's knit_root_dir); when the chunks are run one by one outside a knit, from the working directory, which must then
# hold the notebook. The bootstrap draws, saved during each did fit, go to a new folder of this R session's temporary directory for
# each knit (a second knit in the same session draws into its own), removed when the session ends
knitting <- !is.null(knitr::current_input())
NOTEBOOK_DIR <- if (knitting) dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)) else "."
if (!knitting && !file.exists(file.path(NOTEBOOK_DIR, "composition.Rmd")))
  stop("the notebook's folder is not known: knit composition.Rmd, or set the working directory to its folder", call. = FALSE)
NOTEBOOK_DIR <- normalizePath(NOTEBOOK_DIR, winslash = "/")
# a full path: a drive, a root, a network share (\\server\share or //server/share), a backslash-led path or the home folder
is_absolute <- function(p) grepl("^(~|/|\\\\|[A-Za-z]:[/\\\\])", p)
stopifnot("is_absolute self-test" =
            identical(is_absolute(c("C:/a", "c:\\a", "/a", "//server/a", "\\\\server\\a", "\\a", "~/a", "output", "./a", "a/b", "C:a")),
                      c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE)))
in_notebook_dir <- function(p) if (is_absolute(p)) path.expand(p) else file.path(NOTEBOOK_DIR, p)
DATA_DIR <- normalizePath(in_notebook_dir(param("data_dir")), winslash = "/", mustWork = FALSE)
if (!dir.exists(DATA_DIR)) stop("the data folder is missing: ", DATA_DIR, call. = FALSE)
output_dir <- normalizePath(in_notebook_dir(param("out_dir")), winslash = "/", mustWork = FALSE)
TAB_DIR <- file.path(output_dir, "tables")
FIG_DIR <- file.path(output_dir, "figures")
NUM_DIR <- file.path(output_dir, "numbers")
BOOT_DIR <- tempfile("composition_draws_")
stopifnot("a new folder for this knit's bootstrap draws" = !file.exists(BOOT_DIR))
for (folder in c(TAB_DIR, FIG_DIR, NUM_DIR, BOOT_DIR))
  dir.create(folder, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
say("notebook folder %s; data folder %s; output folder %s", NOTEBOOK_DIR, DATA_DIR, output_dir)
# a table or macro file of the paper, with the header line first: the lines of `text` (writeLines), or, with lines = FALSE, a
# text that already ends in a line break, as it is (the two tables written with cat)
TEX_HEADER <- "% Generated by composition.Rmd"
write_tex <- function(text, file, lines = TRUE) {
  target <- file.path(TAB_DIR, file)
  if (lines) writeLines(c(TEX_HEADER, text), target) else cat(TEX_HEADER, "\n", text, file = target, sep = "")
  invisible(target)
}

available_cores <- parallel::detectCores(logical = TRUE)

stopifnot(length(N_CORES) == 1L, is.finite(N_CORES), N_CORES >= 1L)
```

## Computing resources

Defines how many worker processes the randomization tests use: as many as the cores allow and the
free memory holds. Each worker scores whole reassignments, and the scores are combined in the
reassignments' order.

```{r computing-resources}
# The memory free for worker processes, in bytes (NA when it cannot be read): on Windows the free
# physical memory; on Linux MemAvailable, bounded by the control group's limit (cgroup v2: memory.max
# less memory.current at every level of the group's path; cgroup v1: memory.limit_in_bytes less
# memory.usage_in_bytes); on macOS the free, inactive, speculative and purgeable pages
available_memory <- function() {
  read_number <- function(f) if (file.exists(f)) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(readLines(f, warn = FALSE)[1L])) else NA_real_
  bytes <- tryCatch({
    os <- Sys.info()[["sysname"]]
    if (os == "Windows") {
      value <- system2("powershell.exe", c("-NoProfile", "-NonInteractive", "-Command",
        shQuote("(Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem).FreePhysicalMemory * 1024")),
        stdout = TRUE, stderr = FALSE)
      as.numeric(tail(value, 1L))
    } else if (os == "Linux") {
      info <- readLines("/proc/meminfo", warn = FALSE)
      available <- as.numeric(sub("^MemAvailable:\\s*([0-9]+).*", "\\1",
        grep("^MemAvailable:", info, value = TRUE))) * 1024
      groups <- readLines("/proc/self/cgroup", warn = FALSE)
      v1 <- grep("^[0-9]+:([^:]+,)?memory(,[^:]+)?:", groups, value = TRUE)
      if (length(v1)) {
        base <- "/sys/fs/cgroup/memory"
        dirs <- unique(c(file.path(base, sub("^/", "", sub("^[^:]*:[^:]*:", "", v1[1L]))), base))
        limit <- vapply(file.path(dirs, "memory.limit_in_bytes"), read_number, 0)
        used <- vapply(file.path(dirs, "memory.usage_in_bytes"), read_number, 0)
        ok <- is.finite(limit) & is.finite(used) & limit < 2^60
        if (any(ok)) available <- min(available, max(0, limit[ok][1L] - used[ok][1L])) else
          message("cgroup v1: no memory limit could be read; using MemAvailable")
        return(available)
      }
      group <- grep("^0::", groups, value = TRUE)
      root <- "/sys/fs/cgroup"
      parts <- if (length(group)) strsplit(sub("^0::/?", "", group[1L]), "/", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]] else character(0)
      parts <- parts[nzchar(parts)]
      dirs <- c(root, if (length(parts)) file.path(root, Reduce(file.path, parts, accumulate = TRUE)))
      limit <- vapply(file.path(dirs, "memory.max"), read_number, 0)         # "max" (no limit) reads as NA
      used <- vapply(file.path(dirs, "memory.current"), read_number, 0)
      readable <- file.exists(file.path(dirs, "memory.max")) & file.exists(file.path(dirs, "memory.current"))
      if (length(group) && !any(readable)) return(NA_real_)
      ok <- is.finite(limit) & is.finite(used)
      if (any(ok)) available <- min(available, max(0, min(limit[ok] - used[ok])))
      available
    } else if (os == "Darwin") {
      info <- system2("/usr/bin/vm_stat", stdout = TRUE, stderr = FALSE)
      page <- as.numeric(sub(".*page size of ([0-9]+) bytes.*", "\\1", info[1L]))
      pages <- function(label) {
        x <- grep(paste0("^", label, ":"), info, value = TRUE)
        if (length(x)) as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9]", "", x[1L])) else 0
      }
      page * sum(vapply(c("Pages free", "Pages inactive", "Pages speculative", "Pages purgeable"), pages, 0))
    } else NA_real_
  }, error = function(e) NA_real_)
  if (length(bytes) != 1L || !is.finite(bytes) || bytes <= 0) NA_real_ else bytes
}

# The number of worker processes for a set of tasks: at most `cores`, and as many as the free memory
# holds after a reserve of a quarter of it (at least 2 GB), given each task's estimated bytes; one
# worker when the free memory cannot be read. Prints the count and the reason
worker_limit <- function(bytes_per_task, cores, label) {
  n <- min(as.integer(cores), length(bytes_per_task))
  available <- available_memory()
  if (!is.finite(available)) {
    say("%s: the free memory could not be read; one worker process", label)
    return(1L)
  }
  budget <- max(0, available - max(2 * 1024^3, .25 * available))
  largest <- sort(bytes_per_task, decreasing = TRUE)
  while (n > 1L && sum(head(largest, n)) > budget) n <- n - 1L
  if (largest[1L] > budget) say("%s: one task's estimated memory exceeds the budget", label)
  say("%s: %d worker process%s (cores %d; free memory %.1f GB, budget %.1f GB, about %.2f GB a task)",
      label, n, if (n == 1L) "" else "es", as.integer(cores), available / 1024^3, budget / 1024^3, largest[1L] / 1024^3)
  n
}
```

## Saved schedules and bootstrap draws

Prints the versions of the packages the bootstrap draws depend on (the setup stops unless R is 4.5.1
and did is 2.1.2, and unless the bootstrap multipliers of a full call from the main seed are these
results') and defines the reader of the 16 files of saved rollout reassignments (9,999 or 2,999
each). Every randomization test of Table II, Figure 2 and Appendix Tables B.3, B.4 and B.7 scores
its saved reassignments. The bootstrap draws are drawn anew and saved in a new folder of the
session's temporary directory while the knit runs.

```{r saved-draws}
stopifnot("the bootstrap draws are drawn anew: their folder starts empty" = length(list.files(BOOT_DIR)) == 0L)

draw_packages <- c("did", "BMisc", "data.table", "DRDID", "Matrix", "Rcpp", "RcppArmadillo")
print(data.table(package = draw_packages,
                 version = vapply(draw_packages, function(p) as.character(packageVersion(p)), "")))

# The saved reassignments of one randomization test: B schedules, each giving the 16 regions the
# observed wave years in a random order (the waves keep their sizes 1, 4, 10 and 1). The saved
# observed waves must equal those computed from the panel. Returns the B schedules (region -> wave)
wave_draws <- function(id, waves, B) {
  stopifnot("a schedule file of the data folder" = id %in% SCHEDULE_IDS)
  saved <- readRDS(input_file(id))
  stopifnot("the schedule's observed waves are the panel's" = identical(saved$observed, waves),
            "the schedule holds B reassignments" = nrow(saved$assignments) == B,
            "one column per region" = identical(colnames(saved$assignments), names(waves)))
  lapply(seq_len(B), function(b) setNames(saved$assignments[b, ], names(waves)))
}

# Evaluates a did call while saving its bootstrap draws: did's internal run_multiplier_bootstrap is
# replaced, for the duration of the call, by a function that draws as did does, saves each draw
# (multipliers by region, deviations, random-number state) to <temporary folder>/<label>_<call>.rds,
# and asserts that the saved multipliers reproduce did's deviations (to 1e-10) from the same
# random-number state; did's function is restored on exit
with_bootstrap_draws <- function(expr, label, regions) {
  prefix <- label
  call_state <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
  call_state$n <- 0L
  namespace <- asNamespace("did")
  original_sampler <- get("run_multiplier_bootstrap", envir = namespace)
  sampler <- function(inf.func, biters, pl = FALSE, cores = 1) {
    call_state$n <- call_state$n + 1L
    filename <- file.path(BOOT_DIR, sprintf("%s_%02d.rds", prefix, call_state$n))
    if (file.exists(filename)) stop("The bootstrap draws are drawn anew; a saved file exists: ", filename)
    before <- .Random.seed
    deviations <- original_sampler(inf.func, biters, pl, cores)
    after <- .Random.seed
    assign(".Random.seed", before, envir = .GlobalEnv)
    n <- nrow(inf.func)
    multipliers <- BMisc::multiplier_bootstrap(diag(n), biters) * n
    stopifnot(identical(.Random.seed, after), n == length(regions),
              max(abs(deviations - multipliers %*% inf.func / n), na.rm = TRUE) < 1e-10)
    assign(".Random.seed", after, envir = .GlobalEnv)
    colnames(multipliers) <- as.character(regions)
    saveRDS(list(id = prefix, call = call_state$n, regions = regions, biters = biters,
                 influence = inf.func, multipliers = multipliers, deviations = deviations,
                 rng_before = before, rng_after = after), filename)
    deviations
  }
  unlockBinding("run_multiplier_bootstrap", namespace)
  assign("run_multiplier_bootstrap", sampler, envir = namespace)
  lockBinding("run_multiplier_bootstrap", namespace)
  on.exit({
    unlockBinding("run_multiplier_bootstrap", namespace)
    assign("run_multiplier_bootstrap", original_sampler, envir = namespace)
    lockBinding("run_multiplier_bootstrap", namespace)
  }, add = TRUE)
  eval(substitute(expr), envir = parent.frame())
}
```

## Estimators and the randomization statistic

Defines the estimators every exhibit uses. Each estimate is did's group-time average effect
(Callaway and Sant'Anna 2021) with not-yet-treated comparison cells, a universal base period ($g-1$),
no anticipation and an unbalanced panel, aggregated by did's `aggte`; its standard error comes from
did's multiplier bootstrap clustered by region. The reference-period specification ("Reference
period $g-2$", Appendix Table B.3's sixth row, a robustness row, and row 6 of the robustness csvs)
sets did's anticipation to one year: each SAE-assigned class is compared with the class of $g-2$,
and the comparison cells in year $t$ are those that adopt after $t+1$ (a cell in the year before its
own adoption is left out); that specification's randomization statistic uses the same base year and
comparison cells. No cell adopts after 2021, so that specification has no comparison cell in 2020:
it estimates the entering classes of 2017-2019 and leaves out the 2020 adoption group. The
significance stars come from randomization
inference: the paired estimate, studentized by its delete-one-region jackknife standard error, is
recomputed under each saved reassignment of the rollout across regions, and the p-value is the share
of reassignments whose statistic is at least as large in absolute value. The did fits (28 in all)
run in one separate R process; its warnings and messages are printed here. With BMisc 1.4.10, the
version these results were run with, each fit prints two warnings that `BMisc::rhs.vars` and
`BMisc::getListElement` are deprecated, two functions did 2.1.2 calls (56 warnings in all); BMisc
1.4.8 prints none and draws the same multipliers.

```{r estimation-functions}
# a number as printed, without the minus sign of a value that rounds to zero ("-0.000" is written "0.000"): the one guard fmt,
# b_num, f2 and h_num format through
no_minus_zero <- function(s) sub("^-(0\\.0+)$", "\\1", s)
stopifnot("no_minus_zero self-test: -0.000, -0.00 and -0.0 lose the sign; -0.001, -1.000, 0.000 and NA stay as they are" =
            identical(no_minus_zero(c("-0.000", "-0.00", "-0.0", "-0.001", "-1.000", "0.000", "NA")),
                      c("0.000", "0.00", "0.0", "-0.001", "-1.000", "0.000", "NA")) &&
            identical(no_minus_zero(sprintf("%.3f", c(-0.0004, 0.0004, -0.0006, NA))), c("0.000", "0.000", "-0.001", "NA")))
fmt  <- function(x) no_minus_zero(sprintf("%.3f", x))
comma_int <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)   # a count with thousands commas
star <- function(p) ifelse(p < .01, "$^{***}$", ifelse(p < .05, "$^{**}$", ifelse(p < .1,  "$^{*}$", "")))
stars_text <- function(p) ifelse(p < .01, "***", ifelse(p < .05, "**", ifelse(p < .1, "*", "")))
row_tex <- function(lbl, vals) paste0("      ", lbl, " & ", paste(vals, collapse = " & "), "\\\\\n")
# a randomization p-value as the paper prints it. Each test returns its p as count / total: count is 1 + the reassignments
# whose statistic is at least the observed one, total is 1 + the reassignments scored (B, less any dropped as undefined). The
# p-value is written with `digits` decimals from these two whole numbers, a tie rounded to the even digit, so every computer
# prints the same digits (printf rounds 2,355 / 3,000 = 0.785, a tie, down on Windows and up on Linux and macOS)
p_count <- function(count, total, digits = 2L) {
  stopifnot("whole numbers, 1 <= count <= total" = !anyNA(count) && !anyNA(total) && all(count == round(count)) &&
              all(total == round(total)) && all(count >= 1) && all(count <= total),
            "one total, or one for each count" = length(total) %in% c(1L, length(count)))
  scale <- 10^digits
  h <- (count * scale) %/% total
  r <- (count * scale) %% total
  h <- h + (2 * r > total | (2 * r == total & h %% 2 == 1))
  sprintf(paste0("%d.%0", digits, "d"), as.integer(h %/% scale), as.integer(h %% scale))
}
stopifnot("p_count self-test, two decimals over 3,000: 2,355 is 0.78 and 2,385 is 0.80 (ties, to the even digit); 2,627 is 0.88" =
            identical(p_count(c(2355, 2385, 2627), 3000), c("0.78", "0.80", "0.88")),
          "p_count self-test, three decimals (as in Appendix Table B.7): over 3,000, 2,627 is 0.876 and 13 is 0.004 (rounded down); over 10,000, 125 is 0.012 (a tie, to the even digit) and 1,234 is 0.123 (rounded down)" =
            identical(p_count(c(2627, 13), 3000, 3L), c("0.876", "0.004")) && identical(p_count(c(125, 1234), 10000, 3L), c("0.012", "0.123")),
          "p_count self-test: 8 of 10,000 is 0.0008; with one of 2,999 reassignments dropped, 1,499 of 2,999 is 0.50; a count equal to its total is 1.00" =
            identical(p_count(8, 10000, 4L), "0.0008") && identical(p_count(1499, 2999), "0.50") && identical(p_count(3000, 3000), "1.00"))

# did's overall effect of SAE on outcome `yvar` in the cell-year panel D (optionally weighted by
# column `weightsname`), with `bit` bootstrap draws and `anticipation` years of anticipation (0; 1 in
# the reference-period specification, "Reference period g-2"); returns the estimate, its SE and the counts, and with
# `effects = TRUE` also `post_effects`, the (g, t) pairs the estimate averages
fit_cs <- function(D, yvar, weightsname = NULL, bit = B_BOOT, id, anticipation = 0L, effects = FALSE) {
  d <- D[!is.na(get(yvar)), c(.(cell_id = cell_id, yr = yr, G = G, region = region, y = get(yvar)),
                              if (!is.null(weightsname)) .(w = get(weightsname)))]
  # effects = TRUE also returns post_effects, the (g, t) pairs of the post-adoption effects the estimate averages, read from
  # did's group-time fit (keep_fit); the estimate, its draws and the random-number stream are the same either way
  estimate <- fit_did(d, id, weightsname = if (!is.null(weightsname)) "w", bit = bit, anticipation = anticipation, keep_fit = effects)
  if (effects) {
    fit <- estimate$fit
    estimate <- list(att = estimate$aggregate$overall.att, se = estimate$aggregate$overall.se)
  }
  stopifnot("a finite estimate and standard error" = is.finite(estimate$att) && is.finite(estimate$se))
  out <- list(att = estimate$att, se = estimate$se, n_cellyears = nrow(d), n_cells = uniqueN(d$cell_id))
  if (effects) {
    post <- fit$t >= fit$group & is.finite(fit$att)
    out$post_effects <- data.table(g = as.integer(fit$group[post]), t = as.integer(fit$t[post]))
  }
  out
}
# the outcome's mean over every cell-year before the cell's adoption year (the tables' "Mean (pre-treatment)")
pre_mean <- function(D, yvar) D[yr < G & !is.na(get(yvar)), mean(get(yvar))]

# each region's wave: the DOOR of its entry grades (DOOR - 1 at the other grades); one wave per region
wave_map <- function(D) {
  WM <- unique(D[, .(region, door, is_entry)])
  WM[, wave := door - (1L - is_entry)]
  stopifnot("one wave per region" = WM[, uniqueN(wave), by = region][, all(V1 == 1L)])
  W <- unique(WM[, .(region, wave)])[order(region)]
  setNames(W$wave, as.character(W$region))
}
# the outcome as a cell x year matrix, with each cell's region, entry status and (optionally) weight
prep_ri <- function(D, yvar, wcol = NULL) {
  d <- D[!is.na(get(yvar))]
  d <- d[, c("cell", "region", "is_entry", "yr", yvar, wcol), with = FALSE]
  setnames(d, yvar, "y")
  Wd <- dcast(d, cell + region + is_entry ~ yr, value.var = "y")
  yrs <- as.integer(setdiff(names(Wd), c("cell", "region", "is_entry")))
  w <- NULL
  if (!is.null(wcol)) {
    wc <- unique(d[, .(cell, wv = get(wcol))])
    w <- wc$wv[match(Wd$cell, wc$cell)]
    stopifnot("one weight per cell, none missing" = !anyDuplicated(wc$cell) && !anyNA(w))
  }
  list(M = as.matrix(Wd[, as.character(yrs), with = FALSE]),
       region = Wd$region, is_entry = Wd$is_entry, yrs = yrs, w = w)
}
ES_LEADS <- -6L:-2L
# The paired leads at g-6 .. g-2 under a rollout: for each adoption group g and lead e, the treated
# cells' mean change from g-1 to g+e less the not-yet-treated cells' mean change, using the cells
# observed in both years, averaged over groups by their treated-cell counts (the joint lead test's statistic)
paired_leads <- function(pp, wv) {
  G <- wv[as.character(pp$region)] + (1L - pp$is_entry) + 1L
  yrs <- pp$yrs; M <- pp$M
  out <- setNames(rep(NA_real_, length(ES_LEADS)), as.character(ES_LEADS))
  for (e in ES_LEADS) {
    num <- 0; den <- 0
    for (g in sort(unique(G))) {
      bi <- match(g - 1L, yrs); ti <- match(g + e, yrs)
      if (is.na(bi) || is.na(ti)) next
      tr <- G == g
      ok_t <- tr & !is.na(M[, ti]) & !is.na(M[, bi])
      ok_c <- (G > g - 1L) & !tr & !is.na(M[, ti]) & !is.na(M[, bi])
      if (!any(ok_t) || !any(ok_c)) next
      att <- mean(M[ok_t, ti] - M[ok_t, bi]) - mean(M[ok_c, ti] - M[ok_c, bi])
      num <- num + sum(ok_t) * att; den <- den + sum(ok_t)
    }
    out[as.character(e)] <- if (den > 0) num / den else NA_real_
  }
  out
}
# The joint randomization test of the leads g-6 .. g-2 (Figure 2): the observed paired leads, each
# divided by its SD across the saved reassignments; the statistic is the largest of the five in
# absolute value, and p is the share of reassignments whose largest is at least as large (p = count /
# total, as p_count reads it). Also counts the reassignments under which a lead could not be computed
ri_pretrend_y <- function(D, yvar, check = NULL, B = B_RI_ROBUST) {
  wv <- wave_map(D); pp <- prep_ri(D, yvar)
  obs <- paired_leads(pp, wv)
  if (!is.null(check))
    stopifnot("the paired leads track did's dynamic leads (within LEADS_TRACK_TOL)" =
                max(abs(obs[names(check)] - check), na.rm = TRUE) < LEADS_TRACK_TOL)
  WPS <- wave_draws(paste0("pretrends_", yvar), wv, B)
  P <- do.call(rbind, score_schedules(WPS, pp, paired_leads))
  sdp <- apply(P, 2, sd, na.rm = TRUE)
  fmax <- apply(abs(P) / rep(sdp, each = B), 1, max, na.rm = TRUE)
  count <- 1 + sum(fmax >= max(abs(obs) / sdp, na.rm = TRUE))
  total <- 1 + length(fmax)
  list(p = count / total, count = count, total = total, n_missing = sum(rowSums(is.na(P)) > 0L))
}

# The pieces of the paired estimate that do not depend on the rollout: for each adoption group g and
# year t >= g, the cells observed in t and in the base year g-1-antic, and their change from the base
# year to t (antic: did's anticipation, 0; 1 in the reference-period specification, "Reference period g-2")
prepare_jackknife <- function(pp, waves, antic = 0L) {
  stopifnot("antic: one whole number of years, 0 or more" =
              length(antic) == 1L && is.numeric(antic) && !is.na(antic) && antic >= 0 && antic == round(antic))
  antic <- as.integer(antic)
  region_index <- match(as.character(pp$region), names(waves))
  stopifnot(!anyNA(region_index))
  groups <- sort(unique(as.vector(outer(unname(waves), 1L - unique(pp$is_entry), `+`)) + 1L))
  pairs <- unlist(lapply(groups, function(g) {
    bi <- match(g - 1L - antic, pp$yrs)
    if (is.na(bi)) return(list())
    lapply(pp$yrs[pp$yrs >= g], function(t) {
      ti <- match(t, pp$yrs)
      valid <- which(!is.na(pp$M[, ti]) & !is.na(pp$M[, bi]))
      list(g = g, t = t, rows = valid, difference = pp$M[valid, ti] - pp$M[valid, bi],
           region = pp$region[valid], weight = if (is.null(pp$w)) NULL else pp$w[valid])
    })
  }), recursive = FALSE)
  list(region_index = region_index, is_entry = pp$is_entry, pairs = pairs,
       regions = sort(unique(pp$region)), antic = antic)
}

# The randomization statistic under a rollout `waves`: th, the paired estimate (each group-time
# effect is the treated cells' mean change less the not-yet-treated cells' mean change, weighted by
# treated-cell counts, or by the cells' weights when given; not yet treated in year t: adopting after
# t + antic), and t, th divided by its delete-one-region jackknife standard error
score_jackknife <- function(prepared, waves) {
  antic <- prepared$antic
  stopifnot("the prepared pairs carry their anticipation" = length(antic) == 1L && !is.na(antic))
  G <- unname(waves)[prepared$region_index] + 2L - prepared$is_entry
  numerator <- denominator <- numeric(length(prepared$regions) + 1L)
  for (pair in prepared$pairs) {
    group <- G[pair$rows]
    treated <- which(group == pair$g)
    control <- which(group > pair$t + antic)
    if (!length(treated) || !length(control)) next
    for (j in seq_along(numerator)) {
      it <- treated; ic <- control
      if (j > 1L) {
        omit <- prepared$regions[j - 1L]
        it <- it[pair$region[it] != omit]
        ic <- ic[pair$region[ic] != omit]
      }
      if (!length(it) || !length(ic)) next
      if (is.null(pair$weight)) {
        att <- mean(pair$difference[it]) - mean(pair$difference[ic])
        weight <- length(it)
      } else {
        att <- weighted.mean(pair$difference[it], pair$weight[it]) -
          weighted.mean(pair$difference[ic], pair$weight[ic])
        weight <- sum(pair$weight[it])
      }
      numerator[j] <- numerator[j] + weight * att
      denominator[j] <- denominator[j] + weight
    }
  }
  estimates <- rep(NA_real_, length(numerator))
  valid <- denominator != 0
  estimates[valid] <- numerator[valid] / denominator[valid]
  loo <- estimates[-1L]
  ok <- !is.na(loo); Rp <- sum(ok)
  variance <- if (Rp >= 2L) (Rp - 1) / Rp * sum((loo[ok] - mean(loo[ok]))^2) else NA_real_
  c(th = estimates[1L], t = estimates[1L] / sqrt(variance))
}
# Self-test of the base year and the comparison cells, on four cells in three regions over 2014-2017, worked out by hand: cell 1
# adopts in 2016 (region 1), cell 2 in 2017 (region 2), cells 3 and 4 in 2018 (region 3); cell 4 has no 2014 value. With antic = 0
# (base g-1, comparisons adopting after t) the effects are 4/3 (g 2016, t 2016), 3 (2016, 2017) and 1 (2017, 2017): th = 16/9,
# and the delete-one-region estimates 1, 2 and 2 give t = 8/3. With antic = 1 (base g-2, comparisons adopting after t + 1) the
# pair (2016, 2016) holds cells 1-3 (cell 4 drops: no 2014 value) with changes 3, 1 and 1; cell 2, adopting in 2017 = t + 1, is
# no comparison, so th = 3 - 1 = 2, and with one delete-one-region estimate defined t is NA. With 2014 outside the years, the
# base of g = 2016 is missing and only the pair (2017, 2017) remains
local({
  toy <- list(M = matrix(c(1, 2, 4, 7,  0, 1, 1, 3,  2, 2, 3, 3,  NA, 5, 6, 8), nrow = 4L, byrow = TRUE),
              region = c(1L, 2L, 3L, 3L), is_entry = rep(1L, 4L), yrs = 2014:2017, w = NULL)
  toy_waves <- c("1" = 2015L, "2" = 2016L, "3" = 2017L)
  base_g1 <- prepare_jackknife(toy, toy_waves)
  base_g2 <- prepare_jackknife(toy, toy_waves, antic = 1L)
  first_g2 <- base_g2$pairs[[1L]]
  score_g2 <- score_jackknife(base_g2, toy_waves)
  short <- toy; short$M <- toy$M[, -1L]; short$yrs <- 2015:2017
  short_g2 <- prepare_jackknife(short, toy_waves, antic = 1L)
  stopifnot(
    "self-test: no anticipation unless asked" = identical(base_g1$antic, 0L) && identical(base_g2$antic, 1L),
    "self-test, antic = 0: th = 16/9 and t = 8/3" = isTRUE(all.equal(unname(score_jackknife(base_g1, toy_waves)), c(16 / 9, 8 / 3))),
    "self-test, antic = 1: the base year is g-2, and the cell without it drops" =
      first_g2$g == 2016L && first_g2$t == 2016L && identical(first_g2$rows, 1:3) && identical(first_g2$difference, c(3, 1, 1)),
    "self-test, antic = 1: the cell adopting at t + 1 is no comparison (th = 2), and t is NA" =
      isTRUE(all.equal(score_g2[["th"]], 2)) && is.na(score_g2[["t"]]),
    "self-test: a base year outside the years leaves its group without pairs" =
      identical(vapply(short_g2$pairs, `[[`, 0L, "g"), 2017L) && identical(vapply(short_g2$pairs, `[[`, 0L, "t"), 2017L),
    "self-test: antic must be one whole number of years" = inherits(try(prepare_jackknife(toy, toy_waves, NA), silent = TRUE), "try-error"))
})

# scores a list of rollout schedules with `score`, in the worker processes when there are several
score_schedules <- function(schedules, prepared, score = score_jackknife) {
  if (is.null(cl)) return(lapply(schedules, function(w) score(prepared, w)))
  environment(score) <- .GlobalEnv
  clusterExport(cl, c("prepared", "score"), envir = environment())
  run <- function(w) score(prepared, w)
  environment(run) <- .GlobalEnv
  parLapplyLB(cl, schedules, run,
    chunk.size = max(1L, ceiling(length(schedules) / (4L * length(cl)))))
}

# The randomization test of one estimate: the observed statistic against its B saved reassignments
# `key`; p counts the reassignments whose |t| is at least the observed |t| (reassignments with an
# undefined statistic are dropped, at most 5%): p = count / total, count = 1 + those reassignments,
# total = 1 + the reassignments kept; `antic` as in prepare_jackknife
score_stream <- function(pp, wv, B, key, antic = 0L) {
  prepared <- prepare_jackknife(pp, wv, antic)
  obs <- score_jackknife(prepared, wv)
  WPS <- wave_draws(key, wv, B)
  RES <- do.call(rbind, score_schedules(WPS, prepared))
  TT <- RES[, "t"]
  finite <- is.finite(TT)
  stopifnot("non-finite draws must stay under 5%" = mean(!finite) <= 0.05)
  count <- 1 + sum(abs(TT[finite]) >= abs(obs["t"]))
  total <- 1 + sum(finite)
  list(th = unname(obs["th"]), t = unname(obs["t"]), p = count / total, count = count, total = total,
       n_dropped = sum(!finite))
}

# One did fit, run in the model process: att_gt, then aggte of `job$type`; did's warnings and
# messages are collected and returned with the result and the random-number state
bootstrap_model <- function(job) {
  assign(".Random.seed", job$rng, envir = .GlobalEnv)
  notes <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
  notes$warnings <- character(0); notes$messages <- character(0)
  value <- withCallingHandlers(
    with_bootstrap_draws({
      fit <- do.call(did::att_gt, job$args)
      aggregate <- did::aggte(fit, type = job$type, na.rm = TRUE)
      if (job$keep_fit) list(fit = fit, aggregate = aggregate) else
        list(att = aggregate$overall.att, se = aggregate$overall.se)
    }, job$id, sort(unique(job$args$data$region))),
    warning = function(w) { notes$warnings <- c(notes$warnings, conditionMessage(w)); invokeRestart("muffleWarning") },
    message = function(m) { notes$messages <- c(notes$messages, conditionMessage(m)); invokeRestart("muffleMessage") })
  list(value = value, rng = .Random.seed, warnings = notes$warnings, messages = notes$messages)
}

# did on the data d (columns cell_id, yr, G, region, y): not-yet-treated comparisons, universal base
# period, `anticipation` years of anticipation (0 unless given; the base period is then g-1-anticipation),
# unbalanced panel, multiplier bootstrap with `bit` draws clustered by region.
# The fit runs in the model process from this process's random-number state, which it then advances
fit_did <- function(d, id, type = "simple", weightsname = NULL, bit = B_BOOT, keep_fit = FALSE, anticipation = 0L) {
  stopifnot("anticipation: one whole number of years, 0 or more" = length(anticipation) == 1L && is.numeric(anticipation) &&
              !is.na(anticipation) && anticipation >= 0 && anticipation == round(anticipation))
  job <- list(id = id, type = type, keep_fit = keep_fit, rng = .Random.seed,
    args = list(yname = "y", tname = "yr", idname = "cell_id", gname = "G",
      data = d, control_group = "notyettreated", panel = TRUE,
      allow_unbalanced_panel = TRUE, base_period = "universal",
      anticipation = anticipation, weightsname = weightsname,
      bstrap = TRUE, biters = bit, clustervars = "region",
      print_details = FALSE))
  result <- tryCatch(clusterCall(model_worker, bootstrap_model, job)[[1L]],
    error = function(e) {
      try(stopCluster(model_worker), silent = TRUE)
      stop(e)
    })
  for (w in unique(result$warnings)) warning(sprintf("did (%s): %s", id, w), call. = FALSE)
  for (m in unique(result$messages)) message(sprintf("did (%s): %s", id, trimws(m)))
  assign(".Random.seed", result$rng, envir = .GlobalEnv)
  result$value
}

# the model process: one separate R process with data.table on one thread, where every did fit runs
model_worker <- makeCluster(1L)
initialize_model <- function(paths) {
  .libPaths(paths)
  library(data.table)
  library(did)
  data.table::setDTthreads(1L)
  NULL
}
environment(initialize_model) <- .GlobalEnv
tryCatch({
clusterCall(model_worker, initialize_model, .libPaths())
model_code <- list(with_bootstrap_draws = with_bootstrap_draws, BOOT_DIR = BOOT_DIR)
environment(model_code$with_bootstrap_draws) <- .GlobalEnv
environment(bootstrap_model) <- .GlobalEnv
clusterExport(model_worker, names(model_code), envir = list2env(model_code))
}, error = function(e) {
  try(stopCluster(model_worker), silent = TRUE)
  stop(e)
})
say("did fits: one model process")

main_workers <- worker_limit(rep(512 * 1024^2 + 4 * as.numeric(object.size(OUT)), N_CORES), N_CORES,
                             "randomization tests of Table II, Figure 2 and Appendix Tables B.3, B.4 and B.7")
cl <- if (main_workers > 1L) makeCluster(main_workers) else NULL
if (!is.null(cl)) {
  clusterEvalQ(cl, { data.table::setDTthreads(1L); NULL })
  worker_code <- list(score_jackknife = score_jackknife, paired_leads = paired_leads, ES_LEADS = ES_LEADS)
  for (name in c("score_jackknife", "paired_leads"))
    environment(worker_code[[name]]) <- .GlobalEnv
  clusterExport(cl, names(worker_code), envir = list2env(worker_code))
}
```

## Analysis sample

Takes the cell-year panel and adds each cell's ID, its adoption year `G = DOOR + 1` and the weight of
the entrant-weighted row (`w_ent`, the cell's mean entrants). Checks that every cell has a region and
a door and that the regions fall in waves of 1, 4, 10 and 1. The cell IDs follow the R session's
collation order of the labels `rbd|cod_nivel` (these results: `English_United States.utf8` on
Windows); another collation orders the cells differently, which can move the last digits of the
estimates and standard errors.

```{r analysis-sample}
CP <- copy(OUT)
CP[, cell := paste(rbd, cod_nivel, sep = "|")]
CP[, cell_id := as.integer(factor(cell))]
CP[, G := door + 1L]
CP[, w_ent := mean(n_ent), by = cell_id]
stopifnot("every cell must carry a region" = !anyNA(CP$region),
          "every cell must carry a treatment door" = !anyNA(CP$door))
wv_real <- wave_map(CP)
stopifnot("wave multiset must be {1,4,10,1}" =
            identical(as.integer(sort(as.vector(table(wv_real)))), c(1L, 1L, 4L, 10L)))
```

## Table II: effects on the entering class

Estimates SAE's effect on entrants' mean prior-year GPA and on the low-income share (Table II,
columns 1 and 2): did's estimate and bootstrap SE, and the randomization test over the 9,999 saved
reassignments `headline`. Writes `numbers/headline.csv`; the table itself is written in the chunk
"Writing Table II and Appendix Tables B.3 and B.4".

```{r composition-effects}
set.seed(SEED_MAIN)
g_reg <- fit_cs(CP, "gpa_z", id = "headline_gpa")
p_reg <- fit_cs(CP, "sh_prio", id = "headline_prio")

pp_g <- prep_ri(CP, "gpa_z")
pp_p <- prep_ri(CP, "sh_prio")
headline_prepared <- list(prepare_jackknife(pp_g, wv_real), prepare_jackknife(pp_p, wv_real))
obs_g <- score_jackknife(headline_prepared[[1L]], wv_real)
obs_p <- score_jackknife(headline_prepared[[2L]], wv_real)
stopifnot("the paired GPA estimate tracks did's" = abs(obs_g["th"] - g_reg$att) < TRACK_TOL[["gpa_z"]],
          "the paired low-income estimate tracks did's" = abs(obs_p["th"] - p_reg$att) < TRACK_TOL[["sh_prio"]])
WPS <- wave_draws("headline", wv_real, B_RI)
# both outcomes are scored under each reassignment: columns th and t of GPA, then of the low-income share
RES <- do.call(rbind, score_schedules(WPS, headline_prepared, function(prepared, w)
  c(score_jackknife(prepared[[1L]], w), score_jackknife(prepared[[2L]], w))))
stopifnot("no draw may be non-finite in the main randomization test" = all(is.finite(RES)))
# each p is count / (1 + B_RI), count = 1 + the reassignments whose |t| is at least the observed |t|
p_g_count <- 1 + sum(abs(RES[, 2]) >= abs(obs_g["t"]))
p_p_count <- 1 + sum(abs(RES[, 4]) >= abs(obs_p["t"]))
p_g <- p_g_count / (1 + B_RI)
p_p <- p_p_count / (1 + B_RI)
cat(sprintf("Randomization test: GPA statistic %+.2f, p %.4f; low-income share statistic %+.2f, p %.4f.\n\n",
            obs_g["t"], p_g, obs_p["t"], p_p))

headline <- data.table(outcome = c("gpa_z", "sh_prio"), att = c(g_reg$att, p_reg$att),
                       se = c(g_reg$se, p_reg$se), p_ri = c(p_g, p_p),
                       pre_mean = c(pre_mean(CP, "gpa_z"), pre_mean(CP, "sh_prio")),
                       n_cellyears = c(g_reg$n_cellyears, p_reg$n_cellyears))
fwrite(headline, file.path(NUM_DIR, "headline.csv"))
print(headline)
```

## Appendix Table B.3, prior-year GPA column: rows 1-6

Re-estimates the GPA effect with the Metropolitan Region dropped, without the cell-years with fewer
than five entrants with a prior-year GPA (the row "Minimum of five entrants"), without the cells the
pre-adoption enrollment check flags (the row "Pre-SAE demand restriction"), with cells weighted by
their entrants, and against the class of $g-2$ (the row "Reference period $g-2$": did's anticipation
of one year, as in "Estimators and the randomization statistic"; it covers the entering classes of
2017-2019): Appendix Table B.3's rows 2-6, its robustness specifications. Rows 2-6 have their own 999
bootstrap draws and 2,999 saved reassignments; row 1 reports Table II's fit and test. Row 1 is also
fitted again with 999 draws and that fit is set aside: rows 2-6 continue its random-number stream in
this order (row 6 last). Prints each row's paired estimate and its difference from did's. Writes
`numbers/gpa_robustness.csv` (next chunk).

```{r gpa-robustness}
set.seed(SEED_ROBUST)
# a: did's anticipation (the reference period is g-1-a)
specs <- list(
  list(lab = "Main estimate",               D = CP,                       w = NULL,    a = 0L, y = "gpa_z"),
  list(lab = "Metropolitan Region dropped", D = CP[region != 13L],        w = NULL,    a = 0L, y = "gpa_z"),
  list(lab = "Minimum of five entrants",    D = CP[n_gpa >= 5L],          w = NULL,    a = 0L, y = "gpa_z"),
  list(lab = "Pre-SAE demand restriction",  D = CP[slack_fail == FALSE],  w = NULL,    a = 0L, y = "gpa_z"),
  list(lab = "Entrant-weighted",            D = CP,                       w = "w_ent", a = 0L, y = "gpa_z"),
  list(lab = "Reference period $g-2$",      D = CP,                       w = NULL,    a = 1L, y = "gpa_z"))
fitb <- lapply(seq_along(specs), function(i) {
  s <- specs[[i]]
  # the reference-period row keeps its post-adoption (g, t) pairs in the fit (effects); the random-number stream is the same either way
  fit_cs(s$D, s$y, weightsname = s$w, bit = B_BOOT_ROBUST, id = paste0("gpa_robustness_", i), anticipation = s$a, effects = s$a > 0L)
})
fitb[[1]] <- g_reg   # row 1 reports Table II's fit
b_att <- vapply(fitb, `[[`, 0, "att"); b_se <- vapply(fitb, `[[`, 0, "se")
b_nobs <- vapply(fitb, `[[`, 0L, "n_cellyears")
b_pre  <- vapply(specs, function(s) pre_mean(s$D, s$y), 0)
b_tests <- lapply(seq_along(specs)[-1L], function(i) {
  s <- specs[[i]]
  score_stream(prep_ri(s$D, s$y, wcol = s$w), wave_map(s$D), B_RI_ROBUST, key = paste0("gpa_robustness_", i), antic = s$a)
})
b_p <- c(p_g, vapply(b_tests, `[[`, 0, "p"))
b_paired <- c(unname(obs_g["th"]), vapply(b_tests, `[[`, 0, "th"))
cat(sprintf("Randomization p by row: %s.\n\n", paste(sprintf("%.4f", b_p), collapse = ", ")))
say("Prior-year GPA, paired estimate by row: %s; less did's: %s (Table II asserts the difference within 0.02 SD at row 1 only)",
    paste(sprintf("%.4f", b_paired), collapse = ", "), paste(sprintf("%+.4f", b_paired - b_att), collapse = ", "))

gpa_robustness <- data.table(att = b_att, se = b_se, p_ri = b_p,
                            pre_mean = b_pre, n_cellyears = b_nobs)
print(cbind(row = vapply(specs, `[[`, "", "lab"), gpa_robustness))
```

## Appendix Table B.3, low-income column: rows 1-6

The same six specifications for the low-income share; the row "Minimum of five entrants" leaves out
the cell-years with fewer than five entrants. As in the GPA column, rows 2-6 have their own draws and
reassignments (row 6, the reference-period specification, last) and row 1 reports Table II's fit and
test. Writes
`numbers/prio_robustness_values.csv` (each row's estimate, SE, the paired estimate, its studentized
statistic and its randomization p) and `numbers/gpa_robustness.csv`.

```{r prioritario-robustness}
t_prio <- proc.time()
set.seed(SEED_ROBUST)   # the low-income fits restart the seed of the GPA column
specs_p <- list(
  list(lab = "Main estimate",               D = CP,                       w = NULL,    a = 0L, y = "sh_prio"),
  list(lab = "Metropolitan Region dropped", D = CP[region != 13L],        w = NULL,    a = 0L, y = "sh_prio"),
  list(lab = "Minimum of five entrants",    D = CP[n_ent >= 5L],          w = NULL,    a = 0L, y = "sh_prio"),
  list(lab = "Pre-SAE demand restriction",  D = CP[slack_fail == FALSE],  w = NULL,    a = 0L, y = "sh_prio"),
  list(lab = "Entrant-weighted",            D = CP,                       w = "w_ent", a = 0L, y = "sh_prio"),
  list(lab = "Reference period $g-2$",      D = CP,                       w = NULL,    a = 1L, y = "sh_prio"))
fitp <- lapply(seq_along(specs_p), function(i) {
  s <- specs_p[[i]]
  fit_cs(s$D, s$y, weightsname = s$w, bit = B_BOOT_ROBUST, id = paste0("prioritario_robustness_", i), anticipation = s$a,
         effects = s$a > 0L)
})
fitp[[1]] <- p_reg   # row 1 reports Table II's fit
q_att <- vapply(fitp, `[[`, 0, "att"); q_se <- vapply(fitp, `[[`, 0, "se")
q_nobs <- vapply(fitp, `[[`, 0L, "n_cellyears")
q_pre  <- vapply(specs_p, function(s) pre_mean(s$D, s$y), 0)
q_tests <- lapply(seq_along(specs_p)[-1L], function(i) {
  s <- specs_p[[i]]
  score_stream(prep_ri(s$D, s$y, wcol = s$w), wave_map(s$D), B_RI_ROBUST, key = paste0("prioritario_robustness_", i), antic = s$a)
})
q_p <- c(p_p, vapply(q_tests, `[[`, 0, "p"))
q_T <- c(unname(obs_p["t"]), vapply(q_tests, `[[`, 0, "t"))
q_drop <- c(0L, vapply(q_tests, `[[`, 0L, "n_dropped"))
q_paired <- c(unname(obs_p["th"]), vapply(q_tests, `[[`, 0, "th"))
say("Low-income share, randomization p by row: %s (%.1f min)",
    paste(sprintf("%.4f", q_p), collapse = ", "), (proc.time() - t_prio)[["elapsed"]] / 60)
say("Low-income share, paired estimate less did's, by row: %s (Table II asserts this within 0.005 at row 1 only)",
    paste(sprintf("%+.4f", q_paired - q_att), collapse = ", "))
resP <- data.table(column = vapply(specs_p, `[[`, "", "lab"), att = q_att, se = q_se,
                   pre_mean = q_pre, n_cellyears = q_nobs, paired_att = q_paired,
                   paired_minus_did = q_paired - q_att, T_stud = q_T, p_ri = q_p,
                   n_dropped = q_drop, draws = c(B_RI, rep(B_RI_ROBUST, length(q_tests))))
print(resP)
fwrite(resP, file.path(NUM_DIR, "prio_robustness_values.csv"))
fwrite(gpa_robustness, file.path(NUM_DIR, "gpa_robustness.csv"))
```

## Figure 2: event studies and the joint tests of the leads

Estimates the effect at each event time (did's dynamic aggregation) for both outcomes, draws Figure
2's two panels from $g-6$ to $g+1$ with pointwise 95% intervals (estimate $\pm$ 1.96 SE), and runs
the joint randomization test of the five leads $g-6$ to $g-2$ over 2,999 saved reassignments. Writes
`figures/alloc_event_study.pdf`, `figures/alloc_event_study_prio.pdf` and `numbers/gpa_leads_check.csv`
(the five GPA leads and whether the largest is under 0.03 SD).

```{r event-studies}
# did's dynamic aggregation of one outcome, its plot (g-6 to g+1, the reference g-1 drawn at zero)
# and its leads g-6 .. g-2
es_one <- function(D, yvar, ylab, fname, seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  d <- D[!is.na(get(yvar)), .(cell_id, yr, G, region, y = get(yvar))]
  estimate <- fit_did(d, paste0("event_study_", yvar), type = "dynamic", keep_fit = TRUE)
  at <- estimate$fit
  ed <- estimate$aggregate
  es <- data.table(e = ed$egt, att = ed$att.egt, se = ed$se.egt)
  print(es[is.finite(att), .(e, att = round(att, 4), se = round(se, 4))])
  leads_did <- es[e %in% -6:-2, setNames(att, as.character(e))]
  es <- es[e >= -6 & e <= 1 & is.finite(att) & is.finite(se)]
  stopifnot("every event time from g-6 to g+1 but the reference g-1 is estimated" =
              identical(as.integer(es$e), c(-6:-2, 0:1)))
  lo <- es$att - 1.96 * es$se; hi <- es$att + 1.96 * es$se
  pdf(fname, width = 7.2, height = 4.8, family = "serif")
  par(mar = c(4.6, 5.0, 1.2, 1.2), las = 1, mgp = c(3.1, 0.8, 0),
      cex.axis = 1.05, cex.lab = 1.2)
  plot(es$e, es$att, type = "n",
       ylim = range(pretty(c(lo, hi))), xlim = c(min(es$e) - 0.4, max(es$e) + 0.4),
       xlab = "Event time (years relative to SAE adoption)", ylab = ylab, xaxt = "n")
  axis(1, at = min(es$e):max(es$e))
  abline(h = 0, col = "black", lwd = 1)
  abline(v = -0.5, col = "black", lty = 2)
  arrows(es$e, lo, es$e, hi, length = 0.045, angle = 90, code = 3, col = "black", lwd = 1.3)
  points(es$e, es$att, pch = 21, bg = "white", col = "black", cex = 1.25, lwd = 1.4)
  points(-1, 0, pch = 21, bg = "white", col = "black", cex = 1.25, lwd = 1.4)
  invisible(dev.off())
  list(leads = leads_did, fit = at, dynamic = ed)
}
j_g <- es_one(CP, "gpa_z", "Effect on entrant prior-GPA (z)",
              file.path(FIG_DIR, "alloc_event_study.pdf"), SEED_MAIN)
rp_g <- ri_pretrend_y(CP, "gpa_z", check = j_g$leads)
cat(sprintf("Figure 2, GPA panel: joint randomization test of the leads g-6 to g-2, p = %s (reassignments with a lead not computed: %d).\n\n",
            p_count(rp_g$count, rp_g$total), rp_g$n_missing))
j_p <- es_one(CP, "sh_prio", "Effect on low-income share",
              file.path(FIG_DIR, "alloc_event_study_prio.pdf"), SEED_PRIO_ES)
rp_p <- ri_pretrend_y(CP, "sh_prio", check = j_p$leads)
cat(sprintf("Figure 2, low-income panel: joint randomization test of the leads g-6 to g-2, p = %s (reassignments with a lead not computed: %d).\n\n",
            p_count(rp_p$count, rp_p$total), rp_p$n_missing))
# the GPA leads, recorded: each lead, the largest in absolute value, and whether it is under 0.03 SD
lead_max <- max(abs(j_g$leads), na.rm = TRUE)
gpa_leads <- data.table(lead = names(j_g$leads), estimate = unname(j_g$leads), largest_abs_lead = lead_max,
                        under_0_03_sd = lead_max < LEAD_LIMIT_SD)
fwrite(gpa_leads, file.path(NUM_DIR, "gpa_leads_check.csv"))
say("GPA leads: %s; largest in absolute value %.4f SD; under 0.03 SD: %s",
    paste(sprintf("%s %+.4f", names(j_g$leads), j_g$leads), collapse = ", "), lead_max, lead_max < LEAD_LIMIT_SD)
```

## Figure 2's points and Appendix Table B.8

Every point Figure 2 plots: the classes the schools selected at $t = g-6$ to $g-2$ and the first two
SAE-assigned classes, with its bootstrap SE, and the joint randomization tests of the leads. The
reference class $g-1$ is zero by construction. Prior-year GPA in SD, the low-income share in
percentage points. The text quotes the two SAE-assigned classes' estimates and the two joint tests
(`numbers/composition_text_numbers.csv`, the macros `AllocES...`). Writes
`tables/appendix_alloc_event_study.tex`, Appendix Table B.8: the two SAE-assigned classes'
estimates ($t = g$ and $g+1$), prior-year GPA in SD with three decimals and the low-income share in
percentage points with one decimal, the precision the text quotes; the text-numbers chunk checks
them against the macros.

```{r event-study-points}
ES_TABLE_E <- c(-6L:-2L, 0L:1L)
es_points <- function(dynamic, scale) {
  i <- match(ES_TABLE_E, dynamic$egt)
  stopifnot("every event time from g-6 to g+1 but the reference g-1 is estimated" =
              !anyNA(i) && all(is.finite(dynamic$att.egt[i])) && all(is.finite(dynamic$se.egt[i])))
  list(att = scale * dynamic$att.egt[i], se = scale * dynamic$se.egt[i])
}
es_gpa <- es_points(j_g$dynamic, 1)
es_prio <- es_points(j_p$dynamic, 100)
es_p <- p_count(c(rp_g$count, rp_p$count), c(rp_g$total, rp_p$total))
cat("Figure 2's points\n")
print(data.table(class = c(sprintf("g%d", ES_TABLE_E[ES_TABLE_E < 0L]), "g", "g+1"),
                 `Prior-year GPA (SD)` = fmt(es_gpa$att), `GPA SE` = sprintf("(%.3f)", es_gpa$se),
                 `Low-income share (pp)` = no_minus_zero(sprintf("%.2f", es_prio$att)), `Low-income SE` = sprintf("(%.2f)", es_prio$se)))
cat(sprintf("Joint test of the five leads: p = %s (GPA), %s (low-income share).\n", es_p[1L], es_p[2L]))

# Appendix Table B.8: Figure 2's points at t = g and g + 1, prior-year GPA with three decimals and the low-income share (pp) with
# one, a minus sign in math mode; the caption, label, column heads, row labels and note are the paper's table's
tex_minus <- function(x) ifelse(startsWith(x, "-"), paste0("$", x, "$"), x)
b8_classes <- ES_TABLE_E %in% 0:1
b8_gpa <- tex_minus(fmt(es_gpa$att[b8_classes]))                                  # never "-0.000"
b8_prio <- tex_minus(no_minus_zero(sprintf("%.1f", es_prio$att[b8_classes])))      # never "-0.0"
b8_note <- paste0("Notes: Estimates discussed in Section~\\ref{sec:allocation-results}, at the precision reported there. ",
                  "The reference is the last school-selected class, $g-1$. Figure~\\ref{fig:alloc_es} reports pointwise 95\\% ",
                  "region-clustered bootstrap intervals. Low-income effects are expressed in percentage points rather than fractions.")
write_tex(c("\\begin{table}[!htbp]", "\\singlespacing\\renewcommand{\\arraystretch}{1.2}", "\\centering",
            "\\caption{Entering-Class Composition in the First Two Years of SAE}", "\\label{tab: alloc event study}", "\\small",
            "\\begin{tabular*}{\\textwidth}{@{\\extracolsep{\\fill}}lcc@{}}", "\\toprule",
            "Entering class & Prior-year GPA (SD) & Low-income share (pp) \\\\", "\\midrule",
            sprintf("First SAE-assigned class ($t=g$) & %s & %s \\\\", b8_gpa[1L], b8_prio[1L]),
            sprintf("Second SAE-assigned class ($t=g+1$) & %s & %s \\\\", b8_gpa[2L], b8_prio[2L]),
            "\\bottomrule", "\\end{tabular*}", "\\par\\smallskip", "\\begin{minipage}{\\textwidth}\\footnotesize", b8_note,
            "\\end{minipage}", "\\end{table}"),
          "appendix_alloc_event_study.tex")
cat("Appendix Table B.8\n")
print(data.table(class = c("First SAE-assigned class (t = g)", "Second SAE-assigned class (t = g + 1)"),
                 `Prior-year GPA (SD)` = fmt(es_gpa$att[b8_classes]),
                 `Low-income share (pp)` = no_minus_zero(sprintf("%.1f", es_prio$att[b8_classes]))))
```
